output.brief: Analyzer B most likely had a one-off QC outlier. The evidence points that way. The repeat of the same vial passed. The other two QC levels and sodium and chloride were fine. There is no 2-2s, R-4s, 4-1s or 10x pattern, and the Level 2 mean did not move after the lot change. Patient samples re-run on Analyzer A agreed within 0.02 mmol/L on average, and the patient median is unchanged. QC ran on schedule, so the staffing suspicion has no support. The cause of the outlier is unproven. A sampling glitch is possible but unconfirmed, so don't record it as confirmed. The Ward 6 highs fit the tube outage better than an analyzer fault. Samples took over 3 h to arrive, half the high results came from Analyzer A, and no repeats were requested. Recommended sign-off: return B to service, close the 186-result review with no amendments, and do not recall, quarantine or widen limits. Optionally add extra Level 2 QC for a week. Ask Ward 6 to recollect fresh samples for high results and to fix the tube route. I did not collect further evidence, so I'm moderately confident, not certain.
